bull.b: Expanding backlog and a sizeable commercial pipeline improve near-term revenue visibility and support continued customer adoption of SteraMist. If management converts advanced opportunities as expected, the installed base and project flow could provide a durable foundation for growth over the next several quarters.

Strong applicator growth can expand the installed equipment base, while rising BIT Solution sales reinforce TOMI’s recurring consumables model. This combination supports a more durable revenue mix than equipment sales alone and may increase customer retention through ongoing system usage.

Solid gross margins combined with lower operating expenses show improving operating leverage as revenue scales. Although TOMI remains loss-making, continued expense control and better conversion of sales into gross profit could narrow losses and strengthen the path toward sustainable profitability.

bear.b: Persistent negative operating and free cash flow means the business is consuming capital rather than funding itself internally. Continued losses reduce financial flexibility and increase the importance of successful revenue execution or additional external financing to sustain operations and growth.

High and recently rising leverage leaves TOMI with less room to absorb operating setbacks or invest through a weaker period. Debt relative to equity also raises refinancing and dilution pressure, making balance-sheet repair important even if operating momentum continues.

The merger’s financing condition creates uncertainty around transaction timing and future capital structure, while regulatory approvals could delay important commercialization opportunities. These dependencies may interrupt strategic execution and make projected growth less certain over the medium term.
